theme: Day after the midterms: Democrats win Congress, bitcoin bounces near $78K in a midterm year that has held up better than most, Strategy's cash reserve covers 38 months, ETH/BTC tests a breakout, Tesla and SpaceX slide premarket on the Texas flip, voters back data center bans, Oracle dilutes, neocloud debt is in focus, and the term premium sits near a 16-year high.

items.title: Bitcoin in midterm years: 2026 vs 2014, 2018 and 2022
items.picked: Democrats won both the House and Senate in Tuesday's midterms. Bitcoin briefly fell to about $75,700 as the results came in, then climbed back near $78,000, per CoinDesk. A story trending on X notes bitcoin rose in the 12 months after each of the last three midterms.
items.matters: Bitcoin has had a weak midterm year every cycle so far, and traders are now looking at whether the post-election pattern repeats. This chart puts 2026 next to the three earlier midterm years on the same calendar.
items.know: Indexed to the prior year-end close = 100, 2026 was at 89.41 on day 305 (Nov 1), the tab's latest point, so bitcoin was about 11% down for the year. The average of 2014, 2018 and 2022 was at 44.79 on the same day and ended those years at 35.41, so 2026 is holding up far better than past midterm years. The median of all years 2014-2025 on day 305 was 166.53.

items.title: Strategy vs every other public company holding bitcoin
items.picked: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said Tether now holds about 150,000 BTC, a story trending on X, and Strategy's Monday 8-K took its stack to 849,327 BTC after buying 811 more, per The Block.
items.matters: Strategy is still the giant among corporate bitcoin holders, and this chart shows how its share has held up as hundreds of new treasury companies bought in.
items.know: The tab's latest point, Oct 14 2026, has Strategy at 848,250 BTC and all other public companies at 455,468 BTC, so Strategy holds 65.1% of the 1.30M BTC public companies own. Its share hit a low of 59.4% at Q4 2025. The tab was last refreshed Oct 19 and excludes private companies such as Tether, ETFs and governments; the image's title still says Oct 7.

items.title: Strategy's USD reserve vs its yearly dividend and interest bill
items.picked: Strategy spent $43.4 million of cash on preferred dividends last week and said its USD Reserve now stands at $4.79 billion, per its Nov 2 8-K and Unchained. STRC dividends also moved to daily payments starting Nov 1.
items.matters: The reserve is the cash buffer that lets Strategy pay preferred dividends and debt interest without selling bitcoin or issuing stock. How many months it covers is the key number for preferred holders.
items.know: In the week ending Oct 30 2026, the tab's latest row, the reserve was $4,833 million against $1,509 million a year of dividends and interest, enough for 38.4 months, the highest in the tab. That is up from 6.1 months on May 29, when the reserve dropped to $871 million. The tab doesn't yet include the Nov 2 8-K's $4.79 billion figure.

items.title: Ether priced in bitcoin: the ETH/BTC ratio since 2019
items.picked: A story trending on X says the ETH/BTC ratio broke a multi-month downtrend near 0.0295 on Nov 3, with traders calling it a possible start of a rotation into altcoins. DeFi tokens led the crypto bounce after the midterms, per CoinDesk.
items.matters: ETH/BTC is the cleanest read on whether money is moving from bitcoin into ether and the wider altcoin market. It has been falling for most of the past five years.
items.know: On the tab's latest weekly point, Oct 30 2026, the ratio was 0.0290, with ether at $2,241.69. Its 2026 high was 0.0347 in the week of Jan 2 and its low 0.0260 on Jun 5, and the all-time high in the tab is 0.084 in December 2021. The data ends Oct 30, so this week's move isn't in it.

items.title: Tesla's drawdown from its record close vs the Nasdaq-100
items.picked: Tesla and SpaceX were down heavily premarket after Democrats flipped Texas's Senate seat and governorship and won Congress, per CNBC. Tesla had already fallen 1.32% to $398.50 on Election Day.
items.matters: Drawdown shows how far Tesla is from its record close and how much harder it falls than the Nasdaq-100 when sentiment turns.
items.know: On the tab's latest weekly close, Oct 30 2026, Tesla was 18.39% below its record close while the Nasdaq-100 was 9.09% below its own. That was Tesla's smallest drawdown since July 10, and well off its 2026 low of 36.47% on Jul 31. The data is weekly and ends Oct 30, so it doesn't include this week's election-day drop.

items.title: SpaceX free cash flow: operating cash flow minus capex
items.picked: SpaceX was lower premarket after the Texas results, per CNBC. It had risen 3.62% to $141.31 on Tuesday on talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile, and on its third-quarter call guided fourth-quarter capex to $35 billion to $40 billion for its AI compute build.
items.matters: Free cash flow shows whether SpaceX's AI and Starship spending is paid for by its own operations or needs outside funding. Capex is now growing much faster than operating cash.
items.know: Over the 12 months to September 2026, the tab has operating cash flow of $15.76 billion and capex of $54.96 billion, for free cash flow of -$39.20 billion. That compares with -$13.95 billion in 2025, -$5.39 billion in 2024 and +$0.11 billion in 2023. The image's footnote still says TTM to Jun 30 2026, but the bar is labeled TTM Sep '26, matching the tab.

items.title: Data-center states pull away: commercial power sales
items.picked: Voters in about 40 localities across 13 states approved data center bans or restrictions on Tuesday, with Ohio seeing the most measures, and Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa called for a moratorium on new data center approvals, per stories trending on X.
items.matters: Commercial power sales are where data center load shows up in the utility data. They show which states' grids are taking the strain that voters are now pushing back on.
items.know: On a 12-month total indexed to December 2019 = 100, the tab's latest month, July 2026, has Virginia at 160.8, Arizona 138.2, Ohio 136.3 and Texas 127.3, against 111.9 for the whole US. Ohio rose from 117.3 to 136.3 in the year to July. The data comes with a lag of a few months, so it ends in July.

items.title: Oracle's share count jumped after a $20 billion stock sale
items.picked: Oracle priced $20 billion of new stock and bonds late Monday, selling 86.2 million shares at $116 plus $10 billion of notes to fund AI data centers, a story trending on X. Its shares fell more than 5%.
items.matters: Oracle is funding its AI buildout partly by issuing stock, which dilutes existing holders. This chart shows how fast its share count has grown.
items.know: Oracle's cover-page share count was 3,024 million on Sep 7 2026, up from 2,880 million on Jun 12 2026 and 2,714 million in June 2023. The tab notes Oracle used its full $20 billion at-the-market program, issuing 141 million shares, in the quarter to Aug 31. This week's 86.2 million share sale isn't in the tab yet.

items.title: Neocloud debt vs cash
items.picked: CoreWeave fell 8.6% to $50.15 on Monday on debt worries, then bounced about 6% Tuesday after Oracle's raise, per Investing.com. The Motley Fool notes its bonds yield 14% to 16%, and it reports earnings Nov 10.
items.matters: The neoclouds borrowed heavily to build AI capacity, and the gap between their debt and their cash shows who is most exposed if funding gets tighter.
items.know: The tab has CoreWeave with $35.6 billion of debt against $5.5 billion of cash, far more than Nebius ($8.5B debt, $8.0B cash), IREN ($7.6B, $5.9B), Applied Digital ($6.3B, $3.0B), Cipher ($5.4B, $0.8B) and TeraWulf ($3.1B, $2.6B). Most figures are as of Jun 30 2026 (Applied Digital Aug 31, TeraWulf Mar 31), so they are a quarter or more old, and CoreWeave's lease liabilities aren't included.

items.title: 10-year term premium vs the 10-year Treasury yield
items.picked: Treasury yields climbed Tuesday, with the 10-year near 4.96%, before dipping overnight as Democrats won Congress, per CNBC and Anadolu. Investors are now weighing what gridlock means for deficits and borrowing.
items.matters: The term premium is the extra yield investors demand for holding long-term bonds instead of rolling short ones. A rising premium pushes up mortgage rates and borrowing costs even if the Fed does nothing.
items.know: On the tab's latest point, Sep 25 2026, the ACM 10-year term premium was 1.02% with the 10-year yield at 5.17%, the highest yield in the tab (which starts in 2007) and the highest premium since March 2010 (1.09%). The term premium was 0.47% in August 2025. The tab is monthly and ends Sep 25, so it is about six weeks stale and the yield has since dropped to near 4.96%.
